names.name: Fry cake
names.said: An old word on an old sign.

text.what: An older American name for the cake donut, still on some signs and menus.
text.story: Historically the terms doughnut, cruller and fry cake were used loosely and argued over. In the older usage a doughnut was raised dough, risen and dropped into fat, while crullers and fried cakes were leavened with baking powder — soda, in colonial times — rolled out and cut with a smaller circle taken from the middle. By that usage it was the fried cake that had the hole.

kin.as: The cake ring that kept the old shape.
The other word in the same argument.

etymology.root: fried + cake: a cake cooked in fat rather than an oven
etymology.note: In older American usage a doughnut was raised dough and a fried cake was the baking-powder ring — and it was the fried cake that had the hole.
